Introduction

The Jefferson County Circuit Court is a state court that operates in Jefferson County, Alabama. It is a trial court that has general jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases within the county. The court consists of 14 judges and serves as the highest court in the county. If you are facing legal issues in Jefferson County, it is important to understand the role and functions of the Circuit Court.

What is Jefferson County Circuit Court?

The Jefferson County Circuit Court is one of the busiest courts in Alabama, with a caseload that includes both civil and criminal cases. The court operates in several divisions, including criminal, civil, family, and juvenile divisions. The court is responsible for hearing and deciding cases that arise within the county.

Jurisdiction of Jefferson County Circuit Court

The jurisdiction of the Jefferson County Circuit Court is established by Alabama law. The court has general jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases within the county. This means that it has the power to hear and decide cases involving any legal matter that falls within its jurisdiction. The court also has appellate jurisdiction over some administrative agency decisions.

Types of Cases Heard in Jefferson County Circuit Court

The Jefferson County Circuit Court hears a wide range of cases, including civil, criminal, family, and juvenile cases. Civil cases may include personal injury claims, contract disputes, and property disputes. Criminal cases may include misdemeanor and felony charges. Family cases may include divorce, child custody, and child support cases. Juvenile cases may include cases involving delinquent children and cases involving children in need of supervision.

How to File a Case in Jefferson County Circuit Court

If you need to file a case in Jefferson County Circuit Court, you will need to follow specific procedures. You will need to prepare and file a complaint or petition with the court, pay the required filing fee, and serve the other party with a copy of the complaint or petition. The court will then schedule a hearing or trial date.

Jefferson County Circuit Court Judges

The Jefferson County Circuit Court has 14 judges who are elected by the people of Jefferson County. The judges serve six-year terms and may be re-elected. The judges hear and decide cases in their assigned divisions, and they also hear and decide appeals from lower courts.

Court Procedures in Jefferson County Circuit Court

The procedures in Jefferson County Circuit Court will vary depending on the type of case being heard. However, there are some general procedures that apply to all cases. These include the filing of pleadings, the discovery process, pre-trial conferences, and the trial itself. The court may also hold hearings on various motions and issues that arise during the case.

Court Records in Jefferson County Circuit Court

All court records in Jefferson County Circuit Court are available to the public, with some exceptions. Court records include pleadings, motions, orders, and other documents filed with the court. The court also maintains a record of all hearings and trials. These records can be accessed through the court.

Filing fees and other court costs are required to be paid when initiating a case or filing any document in Jefferson County Circuit Court.
